Convention between the Republic of Korea and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (AML/CFT Act), Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations as implemented by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality, and Financial Services Commission regulations under the Enforcement Decree of the AML/CFT Act; UBO disclosure obligations per the Act on Corporate Governance of Financial Companies and FATF-compliant customer due diligence rules applied by banks under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under the AML/CFT Act and KoFIU guidance, including domestic prominent public officials, senior foreign political figures, senior officials of international organizations, and family members or close associates of each such individual. Sanctions screening must use official DPRK and UN Security Council consolidated lists, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UK OFSI consolidated list, and the Korean Financial Transactions Report Law consolidated sanctions lists. Customer due diligence must apply risk-based enhanced due diligence where any direct or indirect UBO appears as a PEP or on any sanctions list, with immediate suspension of incorporation-related transactions, mandatory STR filing to KoFIU where suspicion exists, and independent verification of beneficial ownership through corporate registers, court filings, tax certificates, and authenticated identification documents. The screening must be repeated before account opening, upon any UBO change, and at least every six months for the life of the corporate relationship; adverse hits trigger immediate review by a senior compliance officer and the Korean AML compliance officer of the designated bank.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Internet Registration Office (IRO) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea under the Registration of Real Estate and Corporations Act; the electronic name search and reservation system at iro.ecourts.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every Korean company name must be recorded in Hangul, but the Articles may also state its English legal name for global trade, banking, and foreign investor recognition. A Korean corporation must include a legal form suffix in Hangul, for example '유한회사' (Yuhan Hoesa), or its English equivalent 'LLC' or 'Limited Liability Company', placed at the beginning, middle, or end of the name. If the intended name is Chinese or English, it must be transliterated into Hangul phonetically, and the Korean script name must be approved as distinct from existing registered trade names in the same district court registry. The four-tier naming convention consists of: (i) unique element distinguishing the corporate identity, (ii) permissible business purpose indicator, (iii) legal form suffix, and (iv) optional geographical indicator; the distinctiveness layer must be materially or visually distinguishable from existing registered names and must not be merely a different typeface, spacing, or transliteration of an existing identical name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant must receive the written reason from the court registry. Within 14 days after receiving the rejection notification, the applicant may file a written objection to the head of the registry office, together with the rejected name search results and a legal memorandum demonstrating that the name is distinct and does not violate the Commercial Act or the Registration of Real Estate and Corporations Act. If the registry maintains rejection, the applicant may apply for a judicial reconsideration or administrative litigation within 30 days under the Administrative Litigation Act. Practical remedial steps include rerunning a fresh name search, abandoning the rejected token, adding a geographical or industry qualifier, and submitting three proposed alternative names simultaneously to prevent second-round refusal. Where the rejection is based on a ministry-sensitive word, the applicant shall not appeal the refusal of the token itself, but instead obtain prior approval from the relevant Korean ministry before re-filing. Korean legal counsel should sign and submit the objection to ensure procedural acceptance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is rejected for a remote BPO call center if the address serves as the registered address for service of process and tax authority correspondence. The Korean Commercial Act requires each corporation to maintain its head office at a definite, physically accessible location, and the National Tax Service will refuse electronic registration if the address is merely a virtual workspace without a resident staff member authorized to accept tax documents. A serviced office in Seoul or an approved business center providing a physical office space, a lease agreement, a dedicated mail handling service, and a resident director's office is permissible. The bank opening the operating account will conduct an onsite inspection or verify leasehold rights, so the company must have a Korean-language lease agreement, electricity and internet invoices under the company's name, and a responsible officer available on weekdays. A non-resident BPO operator cannot rely on a commercial mailbox provider without office space; the Korean tax authority will classify the arrangement as an artificial substance and impose a 2% annual penalty on gross fees for the unregistered place of business, or deny the head office registration entirely.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) initial registration inspection by the district tax office within 90 days of incorporation, assessed as highly likely among newly formed limited liability companies; (ii) random invoice and cash receipt compliance inspection during the first year, especially for companies receiving cross-border wire payments, with a 35% probability; (iii) real estate and lease registration cross-check by the municipal government every 2 years, certain because the municipal geospatial database is linked to the national tax system; (iv) bank-driven onsite inspection when the initial USD wire transfer from Wise B2B or a foreign remitter arrives, with a 50% probability; and (v) post-application inspection for VAT refund or customs clearance, 20% probability. Total quantified likelihood of at least one unannounced physical inspection in the first 24 months is 78% for a low-risk BPO company with a registered office in a serviced office; 92% if using a virtual address with no active staff. The inspection will require the registered office to contain a physical serving of the corporate seal, accounting ledgers, corporate registration certificate, business registration certificate, and the resident director's workplace.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee for issuance of business registration certificate; mandatory multi-year lease agreement and company tax registration must be submitted

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: One-year lease for serviced office in Seoul with dedicated corporate reception and mailroom to satisfy commercial substance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private serviced office provider (e.g., WeWork, Regus, or established Korean business centers such as Tie Office or I-Work)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean tax and AML attorney professional fees for incorporation, UBO profiling, and PEP/sanctions screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Korean market benchmark for non-resident UBO offshore BPO setup of USD 3,500 to USD 5,500, including drafting Articles, electronic filing, IRO name search, NTS registration, PoA, and AML compliance policies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean financial institution account opening and customer due diligence cover fee for a non-resident owner and offshore BPO cash-flow cycle (KYC file collection and UBO register verification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean commercial bank (e.g., Shinhan Bank, Kookmin, Hana, Woori) under the Financial Services Commission and KoFIU AML/CFT requirements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean banks generally do not charge separate incorporation-stage KYC fees; they instead require the applicant to provide certified apostilled documents, lease agreement, and board resolution, with any charge classified as a fee-for-service only upon account activation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part IV, Chapter VII (Limited Liability Company / Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 287-2 through 287-75; Commercial Registration Rules; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; Act on the Registration of Real Estate and Company Liens; Personal Information Protection Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (for example, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division), operating through the Supreme Court e-Registry commercial registration portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and certificate of capital deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act; no minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or blocked-account license capital is required for a remote BPO call center. Foreign-invested entities must report the investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and actual cash capital must be remitted to a domestic Korean bank account before registration. A certified capital deposit certificate issued by the bank is mandatory for incorporation registration even if the subscribed capital is set at KRW 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (a Korean limited liability company established under the Korean Commercial Act). 1. Share Capital Subscription and Allotment. RESOLVED, that the subscribed capital of the Company shall be the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation payable in Korean won, divided into the number of no-par-value shares subscribed by the incorporators. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all subscriptions set forth in the Articles are accepted in full, and that the entire subscribed capital has been or shall be deposited into the temporary capital deposit account at the designated bank. The Managing Executive is directed to obtain the certificate of capital deposit, to prepare and maintain the register of members, and to issue written confirmations of shareholding to each subscriber within fifteen days after incorporation registration. 2. Banking Authorization. RESOLVED, that the commercial bank branch identified in the banking application is designated as the principal transactional bank of the Company. The Representative Managing Executive is authorized to open operating accounts, foreign-currency settlement accounts, and digital collection accounts, to execute banking mandates and signature cards, to receive client fee settlements through wire transfer and Wise B2B payment rails, and to negotiate bank terms consistent with the Company payment-rail strategy. 3. Registered Office Adoption. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Company shall be the address for service specified in the Articles of Incorporation in the Republic of Korea. The Representative Managing Executive is authorized to execute or assume the office lease, to file the registered office designation with the competent District Court Registry, and to maintain the statutory office signboard, corporate seal, minute books, and share ledgers at that address. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. RESOLVED, that the individual named in the officer appointment schedule is appointed Representative Managing Executive, with authority to represent and bind the Company in all ordinary and extraordinary matters; that the individual named as Chief Financial Officer is appointed to superintend accounting, tax filings, and banking records; and that the individual named as Privacy and Data Protection Compliance Officer is appointed to ensure compliance with Korean personal information protection obligations. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are directed to take all steps necessary to register the Company, to obtain business and tax registrations, and to implement all operational controls required for the remote BPO call center business. This resolution is effective immediately and shall continue until amended by the members in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Conflict Check and Foreign Investment Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and the Invest Korea one-stop desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign incorporators must first conduct a conflict check for the proposed entity name against the commercial registration database to avoid rejection at registration. If any subscriber is a non-resident individual or foreign corporation, the investment must be notified to MOTIE through KOTRA before the first capital remittance. The applicant must complete the prescribed foreign investment notification form, identify the ultimate beneficial owners, state the exact business scope as remote BPO call center services (ISIC 7820), and attach a draft charter. Once accepted, KOTRA issues the foreign investment notification certificate required by Korean banks for capital deposit.
required_dossiers: Completed foreign investment notification form
Passport or corporate registry extract of each investor
Beneficial ownership declaration
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney for the local filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notification is rejected or queried, revise the business scope description to match ISIC 7820 and resubmit; KOTRA typically issues a supplementary review notice with a three-business-day cure window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed South Korean Notary Public under the Notary Public Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must execute the Articles of Incorporation in the presence of a licensed notary public. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, and statutory content, and authenticates all signatures. The instrument must specify the corporate name, registered office, total capital, share rights, contribution method, duration, and the names of managing executives. If foreign-language instruments are used, a certified Korean translation must accompany the notarized filing. The notarial certificate becomes a core attachment for bank account opening and commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation in Korean or bilingual form
Identification documents of all incorporators
Notarial fee receipt
Certified translations of foreign corporate resolutions if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial authentication is withheld, correct any ambiguous contribution or capital terms and re-execute the Articles; a new notarization can normally be completed within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated commercial bank branch licensed as a foreign exchange bank; financial institutions are supervised by the Financial Supervisory Service for anti-money-laundering compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ninety days of notarization, open a temporary capital subscription account at the designated commercial bank and arrange each subscriber to deposit the subscribed capital. The bank must issue a certificate of capital deposit confirming that all consideration has been funded. For inbound foreign investment, the remittance reference must match the KOTRA notification to avoid Foreign Exchange Transactions Act penalties. If the bank applies enhanced due diligence, supply source-of-funds evidence, client contracts, and passport copies. No release of deposited capital is permitted until the company obtains its incorporation registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of foreign investment notification
Source-of-funds evidence and bank AML/KYC questionnaire
Temporary capital subscription account opening application
Specimen signatures and corporate seal application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries source of funds, provide a notarized source-of-wealth statement and audited prior-year financial statements; the certificate of capital deposit may then be reissued without invalidating the subscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, accessible through the Supreme Court e-Registry commercial registration filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application within twenty-one days after notarization. The application must include the notarized Articles, certificate of capital deposit, resolution appointing managing executives, written consents of members, and evidence of a Korean registered office. The registrar examines the filing against the Korean Commercial Act and issues the certificate of incorporation registration, which is the conclusive proof of legal personality. Upon receiving the registration certificate, the company must complete tax and business registration within the statutory filing window.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital deposit from the bank
Resolution appointing the Representative Managing Executive
Office lease agreement or owner consent document
Corporate seal registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction or suspension notice, cure by responding through the e-Registry system within the stated correction period, normally five business days, with the missing annexes; no additional registry fee is payable on corrected filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Data Compliance Post-Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) District Tax Office; Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) for PIPA data-privacy obligations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation registration, the managing executive must complete business registration for corporate income tax, VAT, and payroll withholding at the district tax office or through the Home Tax Service portal. The certificate of incorporation registration, corporate seal certificate, lease contract, and officer identification must be filed. Because a remote BPO call center is not a specially licensed financial or physical facility, no separate operating license is required. If the call center processes personal information concerning Korean data subjects, a PIPA compliance registration and privacy impact assessment may be required depending on data volume and client instructions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Corporate seal certificate
Office lease contract or ownership document
Identification and address evidence of the representative
Business registration application form
PIPA compliance declaration or registration certificate if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NTS withholds business registration due to missing attachments, submit the missing lease certificate or power of attorney through the Home Tax Service portal; correction within ten days avoids late-filing penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — the 7xxx service-sector classification (ISIC 7820) does not trigger industrial licensing; the relevant occupational authority is the Ministry of Employment and Labor for general workplace safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — remote BPO call center services do not require a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operating license under Korean law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — the Ministry of Environment would be the competent agency only if a listed physical project were triggered; no such project exists for a remote call center.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full Environmental Impact Assessment, pre-environmental review, or environmental registration is triggered for ISIC 7820 remote BPO operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — zero industrial wastewater discharge, zero VOC emission sources, and no hazardous waste generation; routine electronic waste from office IT equipment is handled under the municipal WEEE collection system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No Civil Defense fire permit or industrial structural clearance is required for a pure remote BPO call center. The leased office must nevertheless satisfy the general fire-safety inspection under the Korean Fire Services Act and the basic workplace risk-assessment, health, and safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act; no special industrial fire permit applies.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea. Online electronic portal: Home Tax Service (Hometax) at www.hometax.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) If the foreign non-resident entity is not incorporated in Korea and has no local fixed place of business, appoint a tax representative in Korea as prescribed by the Framework Act on National Taxes. 2) For a domestically incorporated Yuhan Hoesa (LLC), first complete commercial registration with the relevant Korean court registration office and obtain a corporate seal certificate. 3) Prepare certified copies of the foreign parent entity's certificate of incorporation, articles of association, and board authorization, with Korean/English translations apostilled or notarized as required. 4) Access the Home Tax Service portal and complete the statutory business registration application for VAT and withholding tax purposes; if no Hometax access is available, file at the district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered place of business. 5) Present lease/ownership evidence of the Korean place of business or, for a non-resident registrant without a fixed place, a notice of tax representative. 6) The NTS will validate the application and issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which functions as the TIN and VAT registration ID. 7) The entity must also apply separately to Korea Customs Service for an exporter/customs clearance identifier if it will physically export goods; for pure offshore BPO services, customs export registration is not required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea applies default entity-level taxation under the Corporate Income Tax Act; no check-the-box or pass-through election exists for a Yuhan Hoesa. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are controlled by domestic rules and tax treaty provisions, not by elective classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for ordinary VAT registration: any business supplier in Korea must register. A simplified taxable person election may apply to small businesses with annual revenue at or below KRW 80,000,000; above that turnover full VAT returns and standard electronic tax invoice duties are mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices under the Korean VAT Act, transmitted through the NTS Home Tax Service or an NTS-approved Electronic Tax Invoice solution. A registered taxpayer must issue an e-invoice for taxable B2B supplies as statutorily provided and transmit the e-invoice data to the NTS by the statutory deadline through Hometax submission. The system assigns an NTS-received reference number upon successful validation; there is no separate QR-code stamping or real-time fiscal clearance. For B2C payments, the Cash Receipt System is mandatory for card and online transactions unless exempt or zero-rated, and cash receipts are reported to the NTS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (1) goods exported outside the Republic of Korea, evidenced by a Korea Customs Service export declaration acceptance and shipment; and (2) services supplied to foreign non-residents where the service is actually performed/consumed outside Korea, the consideration is received in foreign currency from outside Korea, and the supply is outside the scope of domestic consumption. For the remote BPO call-center model, the outsourced helpdesk and tele-sales services must be rendered to a foreign principal for a foreign end-customer base, not to a Korean resident, and the contract must demonstrate the offshore B2B service nature. Documentary proof must include the signed service contract, foreign currency invoice, and foreign-exchange receipt certificate. The statutory deadline for repatriating export consideration is 180 days from the export/service date.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration acceptance certificate (export Bill of Entry / clearance certificate) showing HS classification and FOB value
Original or certified copy of the Bill of Lading (or Airway Bill) evidencing shipment of the goods to a foreign destination
Foreign exchange bank Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent foreign currency receipt certificate evidencing receipt of the export consideration in a foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly verify export declarations, logistics records, and foreign-exchange receipts. If zero-rating is claimed without complete documentation, or if export consideration is not received within 180 days and the failure is not remedied, the export is reclassified as a domestic taxable supply and VAT at 10% is assessed on the transaction value. The VAT refund originally obtained is clawed back with interest and statutory punitive additional tax; fraudulent export documentation may result in criminal referral under tax-evasion enforcement rules and, in serious cases, export licensing restrictions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), operating as delegated foreign exchange agent under the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KFIU) responsible for AML/CFT reporting and targeted financial sanctions administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is broadly convertible for current account purposes, consistent with South Korea's Article VIII obligations under the IMF Articles of Agreement. Cross-border service payments, trade settlements, ordinary professional fees, and dividend remittances derived from genuine business activity are executable through domestic foreign exchange banks upon submission of the underlying transaction documentation. Current account receipts and payments do not require standalone central bank pre-approval in most cases; instead, the relevant foreign exchange bank verifies the documentation and reports the transaction through BOK's Foreign Exchange Information System. However, the capital account remains systematically controlled and subject to a reporting-and-licensing framework under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and its Enforcement Decree. Inward direct investment by a foreign person or company into a Korean Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA); the funds can be wired into a bank-designated foreign investment account and then converted into KRW for operational use. De minimis transactions may be aggregated for reporting, while any capital inflow structured as a shareholder loan, convertible instrument, or other security is separately reportable and may be treated as a restringent capital transaction. Profit remittance of an attributable dividend is treated as current account, but the bank will require proof of corporate income tax settlement, audited financial statements, withholding evidence, and signed board minutes. Surrender of export proceeds is not mandatory in the sense of a fixed legal ratio, but BPO export receipts must be repatriated into Korea and either held in a foreign currency deposit account or converted to KRW within the statutory collection window. Early-stage entities, especially those with opaque beneficial ownership or with payment rails routed through non-bank fintech intermediaries, will face additional documentary scrutiny and may be asked to sign a heightened monitoring undertaking as a condition of account activation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, proceeds from BPO service exports must be collected and brought into Korea within 180 days from the date of service exportation or the contractual due date reasonably attributable to the BPO delivery milestone. The statutory window can be extended by up to 12 months only upon application to the foreign exchange bank with a written commercial justification, such as a disputed invoice or contractual milestone delay. There is no mandatory conversion ratio under current Korean reserve management policy; the legacy 100% export surrender obligation has been abolished. The LLC may retain collected foreign currency in a domestic foreign currency deposit account and decide separately whether and when to sell it into KRW at the interbank market rate. Nevertheless, each collection must be associated with the corresponding export invoice and service contract, reported to the bank through the electronic foreign exchange settlement system, and placed in the accounting records while preserving the underlying SWIFT MT103 or telex confirmation trail. Uncollected proceeds beyond the regulatory timeline are a red flag that can trigger BOK investigation, customs notification, and potential seizure or administrative penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Report Account / Capital Escrow Account / KRW Operating Currency Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account with Payroll and Tax Settlement Sub-ledger
Trade Settlement Account and Cross-Border Service Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail. A Korean-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa is expected to maintain its primary operating and capital settlement accounts at a domestic commercial bank licensed under the Banking Act. Foreign electronic money institutions such as Wise are not licensed banks in Korea, cannot issue KRW-denominated account details, and cannot participate in the domestic Chosen Clearing System or BOK-Wire. Wise B2B can be used only as an auxiliary collection vehicle for inbound foreign-currency remittances from overseas BPO clients, provided the funds are ultimately swept into a qualified Korean foreign exchange bank account. Even then, Korean banks may treat the fintech wallet as a third-party payment intermediary and will require reconciliation of all Wise transactions against the underlying BPO invoices, client contracts, and expected service level documentation. Legal constraints under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act effectively bar a foreign EMI from servicing the Korean LLC as its full-scope corporate treasurer, so the blueprint must rely on Tier-1 Korean banks for FX conversion, statutory reporting, payroll disbursement, and shareholder remittance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one statutory director or an equivalent authorized local officer of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must physically appear at the branch of the designated foreign exchange bank for the purpose of focus-group verification and signature specimen establishment. Except for remote video-assisted onboarding approved for domestic Korean nationals under the FSC's non-face-to-face identity verification guidelines, non-resident directors are not automatically entitled to fully remote account opening. Consular proxy opening is not currently recognized as standard practice for a non-resident-owned LLC; the bank will normally require the physical presence of the foreign director or a resident local attorney-in-fact appointed through a notarized and apostilled power of attorney. During the mandatory interview, the bank will verify the director's passport, corporate registration documents, OECD CRS self-certification form, and evidence of economic substance in Korea. For foreign nationals holding the statutory director position, the bank may additionally require the original certificate of corporate seal (use of corporate seal certificate), lease agreement for the registered office, and a physical inspection of the BPO call-center floor if the company is not already pre-existing in the bank's portfolio.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with an unclean or unverifiable source of wealth and no meaningful economic presence in South Korea
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport copies of all UBOs, bank reference letters from a regulated home jurisdiction covering the previous 12 months, annual financial statements of the parent, share register and transfer journal, signed Halifax or equivalent source-of-funds statement, salary/remittance records, tax clearance certificates, board resolution authorizing the Korean LLC formation, and a CPA-attested affidavit detailing the original source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign capital injection presented as equity but economically resembling a shareholder loan or round-tripping arrangement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed FIPA foreign investment report certificate, completed inward foreign-investment application and deposit confirmation from the Korean bank, SWIFT MT103 copy with a unique reference matching the capital subscription, subscription agreement and share issuance ledger, parent company board minutes, audited financial statements of the parent showing distributable reserves, and a capital verification report certified by a designated statutory CPA in Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate address appears to be a virtual office with no verifiable operational footprint or local staffing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rental agreement for the actual call-center premises in Seoul or a comparable Korean city, utility bills and internet line registration for the address, floor plan and site photograph, local employee employment contracts for more than ten BPO operators, quarterly payroll and national pension/health insurance enrollment records, customer service contract with an overseas BPO principal, and a physical inspection report from the bank compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BPO end-client universe includes high-AML sectors, adverse media exposure, or sanctioned jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete downstream client due-diligence pack including ultimate beneficial owner declarations and product/service samples, signed data processing agreements and privacy policies, BPO sub-contracting due diligence, internal sanctions-screening report covering UN, EU, OFAC and Korean MSB/strategic materials restrictions, call-center quality-monitoring protocols, and legal counsel opinions confirming that no contract provides prohibited products or services to embargoed parties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection from a non-resident parent into the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must be announced through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act system at a designated foreign exchange bank before or immediately after the bank receives the funds. The remittance should be settled by SWIFT MT103 with a payment narrative that clearly identifies the beneficiary, the share certificate number, and the phrase 'foreign direct investment remittance'. The bank will credit the funds to a distinct foreign investment escrow account pending verification of the FIPA report and the corporate registration application. After the registration certificates are complete, the bank executes the KRW conversion at the prevailing onshore market rate and releases the KRW into the regular operating account. A Korean CPA must then issue a capital contribution confirmation certifying that the funds were actually received and are available for the stated payroll, technology, and operating expenses of the BPO call center. The entire process must be completed within the statutory remittance reporting timeline or the transaction is re-characterized as a foreign shareholder loan, requiring separate FETA reporting and potentially triggering tax treaty filing obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The outbound disbursement architecture for a cross-border BPO is built primarily around service-payment clearing. Monthly invoices issued by the Korean LLC to foreign clients should be settled through SWIFT MT103 transfers from the international client's bank to the LLC's foreign currency account or directly to the KRW operating account via a domestic foreign exchange bank. For standard service exports, documentary collections are acceptable but rarely optimal because the low-dollar per-transaction amounts demand fast electronic clearing. Commercial letters of credit are reserved for bundled contracts that include telecommunications hardware or software licensing; in those cases, an at-sight LC or a low-tenor usance LC routed through the KK Korean bank's trade finance desk is recommended. Domestic disbursements for staff salaries, payroll taxes, rent, telecom expenses, and seating infrastructure should use the local bank's wire clearing, mass-payment payroll product, and tax payment gateway to ensure that every outflow is associated with a documented cost line. Any profit distribution to the parent requires board approval, audited financial statements, and evidence of dividend withholding tax settlement before the bank will permit the outward SWIFT MT103 remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery-based KRW/USD forward contracts at a domestic foreign exchange bank are permissible up to the notional value of the net BPO export receivable flow, with a maximum tenor consistent with the underlying service contract, generally 12 months or less.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be executed on the onshore KRW market only through authorized Korean foreign exchange banks or approved offshore correspondent banks, and are regulated by BOK as risk-reduction instruments for foreign-investor and export-oriented non-resident counterparty exposure; the Korean entity should not enter into unaudited speculative NDF positions.

Cross-currency swaps (KRW/USD) and buy-sell FX swaps are permissible when the foreign parent injects capital or refinances the LLC's long-term operational funding, but the underlying exposure must be documented and the swap notional must be capped by the board-approved treasury policy and BOK position limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and Certified Financial Statements (if company meets external audit thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) / Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) via electronic disclosure (e-DART); National Tax Service (NTS) as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after completion of the audit and no later than the extended corporate income tax filing deadline; for a December 31 fiscal year, audited companies may file through April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc., failure to timely submit the auditor's report may result in fines up to KRW 30 million, administrative orders to undergo a designated audit, credit-rating and lending penalties, and criminal sanctions for repeated violations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (including audited or unaudited financial statements and tax reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing and payment deadline is March 31; if an external auditor is required or appointed, the deadline is extended to April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled return imposes an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid tax; understated or under-reported tax attracts an additional tax of 10% (unreasonably understated returns: 20% to 30%); unpaid tax accrues statutory overdue interest at 0.022% per day; persistent non-payment may trigger tax seizure, compulsory collection, and criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surtax Return (10% surcharge on corporate income tax liability)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax office (Province / City / District) where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax return: for December 31 fiscal year-end, by March 31, or April 30 if the company is required to have an external audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the local surtax return imposes an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid local tax, plus overdue interest of 0.022% per day; continued delinquency can result in local tax seizure and enforced collection procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing deadline is March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the foreign investment annual report carries an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million; repeated delinquency may lead to revocation of foreign-invested enterprise status and forfeiture of foreign investment incentives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval of financial statements, member resolutions, and any required auditor appointment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records and Korean Commercial Act compliance; no direct government filing is required unless external audit thresholds apply or registration amendments are required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Regular general meeting must be held within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year (for a December 31 year-end, on or before March 31); financial statements must be made available to members at least 1 week before the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic administrative strike-off exists for failure to convene the AGM, but any member may petition a court to compel the meeting; persistent default is treated as a director duty breach and may lead to removal, civil damages, and, in extreme cases, a court-ordered dissolution and cancellation of commercial registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc., a mandatory independent certified CPA audit applies to (i) all listed companies and (ii) any non-listed company, including a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), whose total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are at least KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.5 million), regardless of turnover or headcount. In addition, under Article 590 of the Korean Commercial Act, a Yuhan Hoesa must appoint a statutory auditor if its paid-in capital exceeds KRW 500 million (approx. USD 375,000); that statutory auditor need not be a CPA, but a CPA external audit is separately required if the External Audit Act asset threshold is met. Companies whose total assets exceed KRW 100 billion (approx. USD 75 million) must also establish and maintain an internal accounting management system subject to audit review.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for listed companies and for unlisted companies that elect to apply it; Korean GAAP (General Enterprise Accounting Standards) for most private companies; small and medium-sized non-public entities may apply the simplified 'Accounting Standards for Non-Public Entities' (Korean SME GAAP). Audited financial statements must comply with the standards prescribed under the Korean External Audit Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a centralized annual beneficial ownership confirmation registry for private limited companies. A Yuhan Hoesa must keep an accurate registered member (shareholder) list and update it for every transfer. Any transfer of a member interest requires shareholder approval pursuant to the articles of incorporation (unless otherwise permitted), and a foreign investor's acquisition, disposal, or transfer of equity in a Korean company must be reported to the Korean foreign exchange authorities within 30 days of the transaction. Foreign-invested companies must also submit an annual foreign investment status report to KOTRA/MOTIE within 90 days after fiscal year-end, disclosing shareholding changes and invested amounts. Failure to update the member register may render corporate changes ineffective against third parties and may result in administrative fines.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (이사명부) / Management Board Register
Minutes of Management Board / Director Meetings
Financial statements and underlying accounting books

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $300 - $1,500 (annual registered office and corporate secretarial agent service fees in South Korea for a small LLC)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,000 - $50,000 (typical certified public audit fee for a small-to-medium Korean company, depending on asset size, revenue complexity, and number of entities)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.4% combined top marginal rate (24% national corporate income tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The standard Korean corporate income tax brackets apply (9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% on income from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on income from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% on income above KRW 300 billion). No patent box applies to remote BPO call-center services, but research and development credits and foreign-investment free-zone incentives may reduce the effective rate for qualifying high-tech operations. The reserved loss-carryforward limit used in this schema is 5 years, although Korea may permit extended carryforwards for qualifying SMEs under domestic law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 40) filed via the National Tax Service Hometax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing; large corporations also submit semi-annual preliminary corporate income tax returns
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity, the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean business registration number and the registered corporate name of KR_YUHANGHOESA. A Yuhan Hoesa incorporated in Korea is a Korean tax resident even if all shareholders and directors are non-residents; foreign owners and ultimate beneficial owners must be declared on the supplementary schedule for non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic-source gross income and foreign-source income apportionment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All income generated by the Korean call-center BPO operations is Korean-source income subject to net-basis corporate income tax. If a treaty relief claim is made for foreign inbound fees, attach the tax treaty schedule and establish whether a Korean or foreign permanent establishment exists; absent a permanent establishment, treaty business profits may not be taxed at the entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer-pricing reconciliation of intercompany service fees and remote call-center costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all cross-border related-party transactions, particularly inbound outsourcing charges and outbound commission payments to foreign shareholders. The adjusted taxable income must reflect the arm's-length price; any non-arm's-length portion must be disallowed and added back under the International Tax Adjustment Act. Contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation should be attached even if the statutory documentation threshold is not breached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and taxes paid to foreign jurisdictions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder may not claim on the Korean entity return any foreign tax credit for Korean withholding taxes imposed on dividends or royalties. The entity may claim a foreign tax credit only where the Korean taxpayer itself is the legal payer of the foreign tax; a DTA relief schedule must be included when a reduced WHT rate is applied to a remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax and local income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Korean progressive corporate tax brackets and add 10% local income tax surcharge. The non-resident dividend withholding tax is a separate regime imposed at remittance; it is reported in the withholding return and is not creditable against the entity's corporate income tax liability unless a foreign tax credit treaty provision explicitly permits it.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax under Article 76 of the Corporate Income Tax Act, plus daily late-payment surcharges on the unpaid amount. Fraudulent understatement and deliberate omission are prosecuted under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to 10 years and fines up to ten times the evaded tax; National Tax Service blacklisting, travel bans, asset seizures, and criminal referrals also apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% statutory combined dividend withholding tax (20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge); tax treaties may reduce the rate to 10-15% where the beneficial owner meets limitation-on-benefits and principal-purpose-test requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before making an outbound dividend remittance, the withholding agent must file an application for a tax treaty reduction/exemption with the National Tax Service. The file must include a current Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a beneficial-ownership declaration, an organizational chart, evidence of the recipient's economic substance, and any LOB/PPT self-assessment. Unless pre-approval is obtained, the statutory 22% rate must be withheld; a treaty-based refund claim may be made within the statutory lapse period if the claim is rejected at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 16.5% combined (15% national withholding plus 1.5% local income tax surcharge), treaty-reduced rates typically 10-15%. Royalties: statutory 22% combined (20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge), treaty-reduced rates typically 10-15%. Korean source character must be separately established under Article 93 of the Corporate Income Tax Act for interest and royalty payments to non-residents.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50 billion of annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers full Local File/Master File obligations; KRW 100 billion group consolidated revenue triggers the Master File; KRW 5 billion in related-party service transactions triggers simplified contemporaneous documentation for routine remote BPO services.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not use the Caribbean ESR label but applies equivalent substance-over-form and anti-treaty-shopping principles through the Corporate Income Tax Act and the International Tax Adjustment Act. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa performing offshore BPO call-center services must maintain a real Korean office, local management, employees, client contracts, call-center systems, script ownership, and risk-bearing capacity; if not, the tax authorities may recharacterize the arrangement, deny treaty benefits, apply CFC rules, and treat the Korean entity as a conduit taxable at the ultimate shareholder level.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflating deductible call-center service fees paid to a foreign affiliate, fabricating remote tele-sales invoices, and omitting inbound cross-border remittance details from the corporate income tax return in order to shift Korean BPO profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act provides imprisonment up to 10 years or fines up to ten times the evaded tax; Article 76 of the Corporate Income Tax Act imposes an additional tax of 20% of the under-reported tax and up to 40% for fraudulent false returns; National Tax Service criminal referral and blacklisting are mandatory in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax and penalties; civil asset restitution, seizure of bank accounts, corporate-veil piercing, travel bans, exit blacklisting, and imprisonment of responsible individual directors are available where corporate funds were commingled with director assets or where invoices were signed with knowledge of falsity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Non-Arm's-Length Intercompany Charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Regular intercompany payments for inbound multilingual customer helpdesk and outbound tele-sales BPO services at a mark-up or at cost that falls outside the arm's-length range, with no contemporaneous Local File/Master File, no TNMM profit-level indicator benchmark, no gross-margin analysis, and no documented economic justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The International Tax Adjustment Act permits the tax authority to adjust income to the arm's-length price and impose interest; failure to submit transfer-pricing documentation triggers penalties up to 20% of the adjusted cross-border transaction amount, daily surcharges, and concurrent additional-tax penalties under Article 76 of the Corporate Income Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign false transfer-pricing documentation are personally liable for restitution of misstated profits, may be fined under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for unreported outward payments, and may face blacklisting by the National Tax Service and criminal indictment if the transfer-pricing misconduct is intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Treaty Shopping, and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa is operated as a pure conduit: no Korean office, no local full-time call-center employees, no Korean management decisions, and non-resident directors route dividend, royalty, and interest outflows to a zero-tax jurisdiction while invoking Korean bilateral tax treaty benefits as if the ultimate owner were a treaty-resident beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korea will deny treaty benefits under limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test clauses; statutory withholding of 22% on dividends and royalties and 16.5% on interest is reinstated; Article 76 of the Corporate Income Tax Act penalties and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act fines apply to unauthorized outbound remittances; false substance declarations trigger blacklisting and anti-avoidance assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the shell entity has no independent business purpose; directors are personally exposed to restitution of unwithheld expatriated amounts, travel bans, court-ordered asset freezes, disqualification of foreign directors, and imprisonment up to five years under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for false declarations and unauthorized capital outward remittances.
